mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases the cost of capital for corporations, compressing equity valuations and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of observations where FEDFUNDS is above the 50th percentile, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 5.0%, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce corporate earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances (UNRATE > 5.0%), or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 3.0% annualized signals persistent inflation that triggers monetary policy tightening expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening economic cycle, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect (INDPRO decline and UNRATE rise) fails to produce negative returns in more than 40% of cases, or the joint signal has a Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 1.5%), a rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals inflationary pressures that lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of observations where FEDFUNDS > 1.5% and CPIAUCSL rises, or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (HOUST > 1600 thousand units), a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market overheating and impending recession, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances (HOUST > 1600 and UNRATE rise), or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising labor force employment (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening economic activity and corporate hiring, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of observations where PAYEMS is above the 50th percentile, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1600 thousand units, it signals robust consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered instances (HOUST > 1600), or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
